header.stance: 油價推高政策回應預期

zh-TW.long_thesis_markdown:
## 油價推升9月升息預期，美債短端領跌

荷姆茲周邊再遭攻擊，兩大原油指標同步大漲，美債重新轉為熊市趨平。2年期殖利率上升5個基點至4.39%，5年期升6個基點至4.55%，幅度大於10年期的4個基點至4.79%，以及30年期的2個基點至5.27%。2s10s收窄至40個基點，2s30s收窄至88。

與週一不同，10年期這次全由通膨補償推升。損益兩平通膨率上漲4個基點至2.35%，實質殖利率維持2.44%。美國新一輪空襲、伊朗報復，以及兩艘試圖離開海峽的油輪遭彈體擊中，使WTI上漲5.83%至$90.76，布蘭特漲5.23%至$95.22。市場提高政策回應預期，美元漲0.24%，黃金跌1.21%。

製造業放緩但投入成本仍高，職缺小增，聯準會理事Barr表示，通膨若未降溫就應果斷行動。期貨反映9月升息機率接近70%。資料並未顯示經濟全面加速，卻也沒有讓聯準會放心：動能轉弱，尚未帶來足夠價格改善。

S&P 500下跌0.71%，Nasdaq 100跌1.29%，半導體跌2.14%，VIX為16.34。美國投資級及強勢貨幣新興債利差小幅走寬，高收益更明顯。海外方面，日本10年期標售在約3%找到買方，沙烏地阿拉伯完成需求充足的伊斯蘭債，塞內加爾IMF初步協議卻使重整更具體。市場仍可提供融資，但條件及底層風險差異很大。

## 製造業放緩，成本卻未明顯鬆動

8月ISM製造業從55.6降至54.6，低於預估55.2，新訂單減少3點至53.7；支付價格維持71.1，供應商交貨升至59.3。受訪企業表示，鋁、鋼、銅、電氣產品、燃料、記憶體及半導體成本波動或上升，多項也面臨短缺。活動放慢，尚未使投入品更便宜或更容易取得。

物流經理人指數由68.9降至66.6，仍在擴張區間。Redbook同店銷售年增率從9.1%加速至9.6%；職缺由718萬增至727萬，略低於731萬預估。合併來看，製造業動能降溫，勞動需求仍穩，名目零售支出也強。

Barr認為，能否等待取決於通膨是否朝2%下降；若進展不足，升息就是適當回應。這位相對中間派的理事，為7月三名支持升息的異議官員增加聲援，但未承諾9月15至16日的結果。市場機率接近70%，仍留有相當空間再次維持利率。

一週以來，2年期殖利率上升22個基點，10年期升15、30年期升10；但30年期5.27%仍與一個月前相同。財政部較大規模回購將自9月9日開始，至少為先前的兩倍，有助舊券流動性；同時，通膨、政府借款與競爭性的企業發債，仍影響私人買方要求的殖利率。

高收益利差較明顯走寬，顯示低品質借款人更敏感。股票跌勢也集中於利率敏感的成長類股，雖然S&P 500跌幅仍不到1%。信用市場的關鍵不只是能否發債，而是哪類借款人可以不必大幅提高成本，就維持融資管道。

## 日本3%標售吸引需求，預算申請仍擴大

日本10年期殖利率1996年以來首次達3%，盤中最多上升6個基點，約一年內翻倍。2年期達1.81%，5年期創紀錄2.265%，20年期3.885%，30年期則接近約4.18%的紀錄收盤水準。

基準券標售改善，投標倍數由2.56升至3.29，接近12個月平均3.26，尾差也收窄，三菱日聯摩根士丹利承接22%。需求優於前一週2年券，但30年期仍須在週四面對供給，承擔更多財政不確定性與存續期間風險。

美國財政部對Bessent與植田會面的說明，支持日本採取果斷市場及貨幣行動，處理日圓明顯低估，並將匯率疲弱與通膨相連；也要求溝通能錨定預期、避免過度匯率波動。交換市場反映9月17至18日升息機率約99%，超過一個月前的兩倍。

財相片山皋月否認曾與Bessent討論貨幣政策操作，強調日本央行權責。日圓在相關報導後短暫走強，隨後貶破160。先前公布的創紀錄¥15.4兆、約$964億干預，仍未確保持續反彈，使國內利率路徑及財政前景持續成為焦點。

18個部會及機關申請合計約¥143兆，對照本年度初始及先前追加預算約¥140.6兆。部分增幅反映高市將支出放進例行預算、而非之後追加的做法，因此不是同口徑的財政擴張。即使使用較廣比較，仍是疫情以來最大申請，未設上限的成長策略項目也可能在定案前增加。財務省申請創紀錄的¥36.6兆債務本息支出，高市仍希望新發債低於¥40兆。

幾乎確定的升息定價、改善的基準券標售，以及未解的超長端供給，可以同時存在。國內公債對銀行及壽險愈來愈有吸引力，但週二需求並未替殖利率曲線設下上限，也未解決最終預算財源。

## 歐洲整體通膨升、核心降，以色列反向降息

歐元區8月通膨由2.9%升至3.3%，為近三年最高；核心卻由2.5%降至2.4%，服務由3.3%降至3.0%。市場完全反映9月10日存款利率升25個基點至2.50%，內部數據卻讓之後的路徑不那麼明確。

Nagel歡迎核心及服務降溫，表示其中尚未看到第二輪效應，同時認為近期決策可預測。立陶宛的Gediminas Simkus則主張9月還不夠，理由是天然氣、農產品價格及超預期活動。市場反映其後一年再升兩次，比部分官員與經濟學家認為必要的幅度更大。

英債調整更急。10年期殖利率盤中最多升11個基點至5.25%，30年期達5.89%，創1998年以來最高；交易員預期2月前升息兩次。Catherine Mann表示成長增強、就業似乎穩定、通膨略高於預期，她寧願承擔利率短暫過高的風險，也不願放任通膨持續。

家庭融資資料卻沒那麼令人放心。7月房貸核准由58,215筆降至56,053筆，低於59,400筆預估，為2024年1月以來最少。平均2年固定房貸利率從戰前4.83%升至5.59%。Nationwide 8月房價上升0.2%至£275,465，優於預估0.1%及前期修正後下跌0.1%，但核准下降顯示交易基礎變薄。消費者新增£20億無擔保借款，存款流入則由£62億降至£38億。

以色列連續第三次降息，從3.50%降至3.25%，18名受訪經濟學家僅9人預料到。謝克爾貶至每美元3.02，但仍接近數十年強勢水準。通膨已靠近目標區間中段，官員扣除以色列企業海外生產後，也看到國內活動較弱。第2季GDP從戰爭造成的收縮反彈、年率成長15.4%，並未阻止央行在本地通膨與匯率容許下寬鬆。

巴西第2季GDP成長0.5%，低於前季1.1%，但高於預估0.4%；年增2.0%，也高於1.8%預估。農業增2.8%、服務0.2%、工業0.1%，家庭消費則減0.4%。14%的Selic利率壓抑利率敏感支出，但8月中通膨4.24%仍高於3%目標，選舉相關財政支持也持續。整體成長較強，降低加快降息的迫切性，卻不能把弱消費解讀為應重啟緊縮。

## 沙烏地發債順利，塞內加爾IMF協議使重整更近

沙烏地阿拉伯發行$32.5億5年及10年期伊斯蘭債，訂單高峰逾$150億。10年期定價為美債加80個基點，比初始討論收窄約30個基點。荷姆茲附近油輪遭攻擊、石油部門收縮之際，這筆完成交易仍顯示充足需求；另行報導的至少$80億貸款洽談則仍屬初步階段。

塞內加爾與IMF達成$22億初步協議，表示將依改良版G20共同框架處理債務。2028年歐元債下跌6.9美分至49.44，主權利差從1,651擴大至1,745個基點。未揭露債務曾使先前$18億計畫中止，新協議重啟援助可能，卻也讓債權人讓步更明確。矯正措施、不新增外債拖欠及IMF董事會核准仍是條件；每年近CFA 6兆、約$106億融資需求，也留下重大流動性挑戰。

整體供給背景仍沉重。IMF警告全球公共債務接近GDP 100%、高於戰後高點，G20官員又難以就債務及全球失衡文字達成共識，仍可能以主席聲明取代聯合公報。

韓國提出2027年總發債₩222.8兆，接近目前的紀錄計畫。其中約₩110.7兆償還到期債，₩15.9兆支持造市，淨發債約₩96.3兆。李在明擴張議程與AI投資工具，使支出增加12.8%至₩820.9兆。3年期殖利率升6個基點至3.9%，10年期升9至4.4%，提案仍待國會批准。

芬蘭預計2027年中央政府赤字€124億，比今年少€9億，並削減€10億支出；利息成本卻增加€12億至€44億。加拿大債市相對有韌性，30年期4.15%明顯低於美國5.27%，折讓也大於過去十年平均約70個基點。第2季外資創紀錄買入C$808億加拿大公債，但預估C$653億聯邦赤字及基建支出，使這項比較仍須保留餘地。

印度4至6月經常帳赤字擴大至$42億、占GDP 0.5%，高於一年前修正後$34億、0.4%。商品赤字由$689億升至$861億，國際收支從$45億順差轉為$81億逆差；私人移轉則由$332億升至$429億。央行優惠美元盧比交換，預期可吸引外幣存款及債券融資。

Capri Global尋求首次外幣債$3億至$5億，為3年3個月優先擔保券，初步指引約7.75%，預期評級BB-。先前因高評級銀行供給競爭而延後。6至8月印度貸款機構透過央行窗口發行$121.5億美元債，逾75%來自民營銀行；ICICI一筆5.308%的$5億私募，使其計畫累計達$35.5億。Capri將以不同價格，把這個融資管道延伸至較低評級的非銀行風險。

尚比亞利差由7月30日216收窄至177個基點，今年匯率升16%、本地債回報近37%。投資人看好政策延續、銅價與可能的新IMF支持，即使預算赤字8%、選後仍有針對反對派的法律壓力。烏拉圭披索投資兩年內增為三倍、逾UYU140億，私人存款外幣占比則從2025年3月後的73%降至約69%。截至7月國內發行$21億中，固定利率披索券逾一半，本幣占政府債務也超過57%，擴大了國內融資基礎。

## 信用分歧來自供給、現金流與治理等不同風險

約$1兆、剩餘期限逾三年的非金融投資級債，相對評級交易利差異常偏寬，其中美國約$5,800億、歐洲近$4,000億；但整體高評級平均利差，美國仍約78個基點、歐洲79個基點，接近金融危機後低點。個別問題比平均數顯示的更大。

大型雲端業者部分反映供給與集中度。六大公司已占美國投資級指數約5%，為兩年前的兩倍；摩根資產管理估計低槓桿可再承擔$1.5兆債務，並指出前三大公司的客戶承諾增速高於資本支出。至2030年基建成本估計$5.5兆，超過營運現金流可支應範圍。即使資產負債表強，指數權重增加仍可能要求發行人讓價。

Brightspeed的問題更直接。Apollo支持的寬頻業者，第2季營收下降8.7%至$3.86億後，新增繼續經營疑慮警示。上半年虧損$8.79億，營運現金流出$3.41億，即使6月30日仍有$11.7億現金及$6.77億正營運資金。公司考慮包括ABS在內的融資，債權人也聘請顧問。光纖銷售增加16%、可服務據點逾300萬，鄉村建網卻尚不能自給資金；先前困境交換曾減債$11億、引入$37億資本，仍未解決現金創造問題。

投資級賓士經銷商中升則面臨降評可能。上半年利潤減89%後，2028年美元債7月起殖利率已逾10%；營收減18.5%，新車銷量減17.6%至188,463輛，股價今年跌約63%。標普評級距高收益僅一級。不過CN¥136億現金可涵蓋明年$3.5億聯貸及CN¥10億債券，公司另回購$1.179億2028年券，餘額約$4.82億。流動性提供時間，豪華車經銷業務卻仍承壓。

HDFC執行長Sashidhar Jagdishan意外決定不尋求續任，美元債連跌第五個交易日。2031年6月券達98.504美分，新發行2029年8月及2031年券也跌至最低。HDFC占印度存款近12%，今年股價跌約28%，Nifty Bank僅跌3.3%。穆迪指出意外的交接風險，但有序接班與策略延續可限制信用影響；這是領導信心問題，不是Brightspeed那種已揭露的現金消耗。

中國預售制度改革重新分配完工風險。買款須存入履約保管帳戶，建物封頂後才可預售，延遲交屋則允許買方解約退款。這保護買方，也移除開發商便宜的預收資金，既有過渡案源消化後，可能減少2027年新開工。2025年底預售仍占新屋交易約75%，但成屋交易已超過新屋；相較高峰近90%住宅樓地板面積採預售，體系規模已縮小，開發商與地方政府仍將面對較少預收款及更弱土地需求。

## 接下來看服務業、非農與長債標售

9月3日紐約時間上午10點公布ISM服務業，預估54.3、前值54.1；9月4日上午8:30公布非農，預期增加5.8萬人，前期減少2.3萬，失業率維持4.1%。聘僱與服務價格將顯示，製造業成本壓力是否廣泛到足以支持接近70%的9月升息機率。

週四30年期日債標售接在改善的基準券標售之後，承擔更多財政及存續期間曝險。9月10日歐洲央行須權衡3.3%整體通膨與核心、服務降溫；9月17至18日日本央行則面對幾乎確定的升息定價與弱日圓。預期走得再遠，實際決策仍重要。

美國財政部9月3日公布當月3年、10年及30年期標售規模，9月7日勞動節休市，8日進行3年期、9日10年期增額發行，較大回購也在9日開始。投標將顯示，官方買盤及競爭性企業供給並存時，較高殖利率能否吸引私人需求。

overall_summary.headline: 油價大漲，通膨補償與9月升息機率同步提高
overall_summary.session_narrative:
荷姆茲周邊空襲及油輪遭擊中，使WTI與布蘭特均漲逾5%；10年期實質殖利率維持2.44%。Barr表示等待須以通膨改善為條件，期貨反映9月升息機率接近70%。

ISM降至54.6，支付價格仍71.1，職缺小增至727萬。日本10年期約3%的標售需求改善；歐元區整體通膨升至3.3%，核心卻降至2.4%，以色列則降息。

沙烏地完成$32.5億伊斯蘭債，塞內加爾附條件IMF協議卻使重整更明確。Brightspeed現金消耗、中升獲利崩跌、HDFC領導交接，揭示平均利差偏緊之下各不相同的風險。

long_thesis.english_markdown:
## Oil sends the front end lower as September hike odds rise

Treasuries resumed bear flattening as renewed attacks around Hormuz sent both major crude benchmarks sharply higher. Two-year yields rose 5 basis points to 4.39%, and the 5-year added 6 to 4.55%, outpacing the 10-year's 4-basis-point rise to 4.79% and the 30-year's 2-basis-point increase to 5.27%. Two-to-10-year spreads narrowed to 40 basis points and 2s30s to 88.

Unlike Monday, the 10-year move came entirely through inflation compensation. Breakevens rose 4 basis points to 2.35% while real yields stayed at 2.44%. WTI surged 5.83% to $90.76 and Brent 5.23% to $95.22 after new US strikes, Iranian retaliation and projectile hits on two tankers trying to leave the strait. The dollar gained 0.24% and gold fell 1.21% as markets raised the expected policy response.

Manufacturing slowed but input costs remained high, job openings edged up, and Fed Governor Michael Barr said officials should act decisively if inflation failed to moderate. Futures priced close to a 70% chance of a September increase. The data did not show broad acceleration; they gave the Fed little reassurance that weaker momentum was bringing down prices.

The S&P 500 fell 0.71%, the Nasdaq 100 lost 1.29% and semiconductors declined 2.14%, with VIX at 16.34. US IG and hard-currency EM spreads widened modestly; high yield widened more clearly. Overseas, Japan's 10-year auction found buyers around 3%, Saudi Arabia completed a well-subscribed sukuk, and Senegal's preliminary IMF deal made restructuring more explicit. Funding remained available, but the terms and underlying credit risks varied substantially.

## Slower manufacturing brings little relief on costs

August ISM manufacturing fell to 54.6 from 55.6, below the 55.2 forecast, and new orders dropped 3 points to 53.7. Prices paid stayed at 71.1 and supplier deliveries rose to 59.3. Respondents reported volatile or higher costs for aluminum, steel, copper, electrical goods, fuel, memory and semiconductors, with shortages in several categories. Slower activity was not yet producing cheaper or more readily available inputs.

The Logistics Managers Index eased to 66.6 from 68.9 but remained expansionary. Redbook same-store sales accelerated to 9.6% year over year from 9.1%. Job openings rose to 7.27 million from 7.18 million, just short of the 7.31 million consensus. Taken together, the readings showed moderating manufacturing momentum alongside steady labor demand and strong nominal retail spending.

Barr conditioned patience on inflation moving toward 2%, with an increase appropriate if progress failed. A relatively centrist governor was thus adding support to the position behind July's three pro-hike dissents, without committing to the September 15–16 outcome. Market odds near 70% still left meaningful room for another hold.

Over the week, 2-year yields had risen 22 basis points, versus 15 at ten years and 10 at thirty. Yet the 30-year remained unchanged over a month at 5.27%. Treasury's larger buybacks, due from September 9 at at least twice the previous size, can help liquidity in older bonds while incoming inflation, fiscal borrowing and competing corporate issuance continue to influence the yields private buyers require.

The clearer high-yield widening showed greater sensitivity among lower-quality borrowers. Equity losses were also concentrated in rate-sensitive growth, though the S&P 500 decline remained below 1%. The important credit distinction was not simply whether markets were open, but which borrowers could maintain access without sharply higher costs.

## Japan's 3% auction draws buyers as budget requests expand

Japan's 10-year yield reached 3% for the first time since 1996, rising as much as 6 basis points and roughly doubling over a year. The 2-year reached 1.81%, the 5-year a record 2.265%, the 20-year 3.885%, and the 30-year approached a record close near 4.18%.

The benchmark auction improved. Bid-to-cover rose to 3.29 from 2.56, close to the 12-month average of 3.26, and the tail narrowed. MUFG Morgan Stanley took 22% of the sale. Demand was stronger than at the preceding week's 2-year auction, but the 30-year sector still faced Thursday's supply with more fiscal uncertainty and duration risk.

The US Treasury readout of Bessent's meeting with Ueda supported decisive Japanese market and monetary action against substantial yen undervaluation, linking currency weakness to inflation. It also called for communication that anchors expectations and avoids excessive exchange-rate volatility. Swaps priced roughly a 99% chance of a September 17–18 BOJ increase, more than twice the odds a month earlier.

Finance Minister Satsuki Katayama denied discussing monetary-policy conduct with Bessent and emphasized the BOJ's authority. The yen weakened through 160 after briefly strengthening on the reports. The record ¥15.4 trillion, or $96.4 billion, of intervention disclosed earlier had not secured a lasting recovery, leaving the domestic rate path and fiscal outlook in focus.

Requests from 18 ministries and agencies totaled about ¥143 trillion, compared with roughly ¥140.6 trillion across the current initial and prior supplementary budgets. Part of the increase reflects Takaichi's effort to put spending into the regular budget rather than add it later, so the headline is not a like-for-like fiscal expansion. Even on the broader comparison, it is the largest request since the pandemic, with uncapped growth-strategy items that could increase before finalization. The Finance Ministry requested record debt service of ¥36.6 trillion; Takaichi still aims to keep new bond issuance below ¥40 trillion.

A near-certain hike, an improved benchmark auction and unresolved super-long supply can coexist. Domestic yields are becoming more attractive to banks and insurers, but Tuesday's demand did not establish a ceiling for the curve or settle how the final budget will be funded.

## European headline inflation rises as core eases; Israel cuts

Euro-area August inflation accelerated to 3.3% from 2.9%, its highest in almost three years. Core slowed to 2.4% from 2.5%, and services to 3.0% from 3.3%. Markets fully priced a September 10 increase of 25 basis points in the deposit rate to 2.50%, but the internal data left the path beyond that less clear.

Joachim Nagel welcomed easing core and services prices and said second-round effects were not visible there, even while calling the near-term decision predictable. Lithuania's Gediminas Simkus argued September would not be enough, citing gas and agricultural prices and stronger-than-expected activity. Markets priced two further increases over the following year, more than some officials and economists thought necessary.

UK bonds suffered a steeper adjustment. Ten-year gilt yields rose as much as 11 basis points to 5.25%, and the 30-year reached 5.89%, its highest since 1998. Traders priced two BOE increases by February. Catherine Mann said growth had strengthened, the labor market seemed to be stabilizing and inflation was somewhat firmer than expected; she preferred the risk of temporarily setting rates modestly too high to allowing inflation to persist.

Household financing data were less reassuring. July mortgage approvals fell to 56,053 from 58,215, below a 59,400 forecast and the lowest since January 2024. Average 2-year fixed mortgage rates rose to 5.59% from 4.83% before the war. Nationwide's August house-price measure increased 0.2% to £275,465, versus a 0.1% forecast and a revised 0.1% prior decline, but fewer approvals indicated a thinner transaction base. Consumers added £2 billion of unsecured borrowing as deposit inflows slowed to £3.8 billion from £6.2 billion.

Israel cut for a third consecutive meeting, lowering rates to 3.25% from 3.50%; only nine of 18 surveyed economists had expected easing. The shekel weakened to 3.02 per dollar but stayed near multi-decade strength. Inflation had moved toward the middle of its target range, and officials saw softer domestic activity after excluding production abroad by Israeli companies. A 15.4% annualized Q2 rebound from war-related contraction did not prevent easing when local inflation and currency conditions allowed it.

Brazil's Q2 GDP grew 0.5%, down from 1.1% but above the 0.4% estimate; annual growth was 2.0% versus 1.8% expected. Agriculture rose 2.8%, services 0.2% and industry 0.1%, while household consumption fell 0.4%. Selic at 14% was weighing on rate-sensitive spending, although mid-August inflation of 4.24% remained above the 3% target and election-related fiscal support continued. Better headline growth reduced urgency for faster cuts without making weak consumption a case for renewed tightening.

## Saudi issuance clears; Senegal's IMF agreement brings restructuring closer

Saudi Arabia sold $3.25 billion of 5- and 10-year sukuk with peak orders above $15 billion. The 10-year priced 80 basis points over Treasuries, about 30 tighter than initial discussion. The completed sale demonstrated demand despite tanker attacks near Hormuz and an oil-sector contraction. The separately reported talks for at least an $8 billion loan remained preliminary.

Senegal reached a preliminary $2.2 billion IMF agreement and said it would pursue debt treatment under an improved G20 Common Framework. Its euro 2028 bond fell 6.9 cents to 49.44, and the sovereign spread jumped to 1,745 basis points from 1,651. The agreement reopened the prospect of support after undisclosed debt halted the earlier $1.8 billion program, but also made creditor concessions more explicit. Corrective measures, no new external arrears and IMF board approval remain conditions. Annual financing needs near 6 trillion CFA francs, or $10.6 billion, leave a substantial liquidity challenge.

The wider supply backdrop remained heavy. The IMF warned that global public debt was approaching 100% of GDP, above postwar highs, while G20 officials struggled to agree on language covering debt and global imbalances. A chair's statement rather than a joint communique remained possible.

South Korea proposed 222.8 trillion won of gross 2027 bond issuance, close to the current record plan. About 110.7 trillion would refinance maturities and 15.9 trillion support market-making, leaving roughly 96.3 trillion net issuance. Spending would rise 12.8% to 820.9 trillion under Lee Jae Myung's expansionary agenda and AI investment vehicle. Three-year yields rose 6 basis points to 3.9%, and the 10-year 9 to 4.4%. Parliament still has to approve the proposal.

Finland planned a €12.4 billion central-government deficit for 2027, €0.9 billion lower than this year, with €1 billion of cuts. Interest costs nonetheless rise €1.2 billion to €4.4 billion. Canada showed relative bond resilience: the 30-year yielded 4.15%, well below the US 5.27% and a larger discount than the roughly 70-basis-point decade average. Foreign buyers purchased a record C$80.8 billion of Canadian government bonds in Q2, although a projected C$65.3 billion federal deficit and infrastructure spending temper the comparison.

India's April–June current-account deficit widened to $4.2 billion, or 0.5% of GDP, from a revised $3.4 billion, or 0.4%, a year earlier. The goods deficit rose to $86.1 billion from $68.9 billion, and the balance of payments swung to an $8.1 billion deficit from a $4.5 billion surplus. Private transfers increased to $42.9 billion from $33.2 billion. Discounted RBI dollar-rupee swaps are expected to encourage foreign-currency deposits and bond funding.

Capri Global sought $300 million–$500 million for its first foreign-currency bond, a senior-secured 3-year-and-3-month issue guided around 7.75% with an expected BB- rating. It had delayed an earlier attempt amid competing higher-rated bank supply. Indian lenders raised $12.15 billion in dollar bonds under the RBI window during June–August, over 75% from private banks. ICICI's $500 million private placement at 5.308% brought its program issuance to $3.55 billion. Capri would extend that access to lower-rated non-bank risk at a different price.

Zambia's spread narrowed to 177 basis points from 216 on July 30, its currency gained 16% this year and local bonds returned almost 37%. Investors favored policy continuity, copper and a possible IMF anchor despite an 8% budget deficit and post-election legal pressure on the opposition. Uruguay's peso investments tripled in two years to over 14 billion pesos, while foreign currency's share of private deposits declined from 73% after March 2025 to about 69%. Fixed-rate peso paper made up over half of $2.1 billion domestic issuance through July, and local currency exceeded 57% of government debt, broadening its domestic funding base.

## Credit dispersion reflects different supply, cash-flow and governance risks

About $1 trillion of nonfinancial IG bonds with more than three years remaining traded unusually wide for their ratings—roughly $580 billion in the US and nearly $400 billion in Europe. Average high-grade spreads were still near 78 basis points in the US and 79 in Europe, close to post-crisis tights. Individual problems were much larger than those averages suggested.

For hyperscalers, supply and concentration were part of the explanation. The six largest accounted for about 5% of the US IG index, twice their weight two years earlier. JPMorgan Asset Management estimated low leverage could support another $1.5 trillion of debt and noted customer commitments at the three largest were growing faster than capital spending. Infrastructure costs estimated at $5.5 trillion through 2030 exceeded operating cash-flow capacity. Growing index weights can require price concessions even where balance sheets remain strong.

Brightspeed's problem was more directly financial. The Apollo-backed broadband company added a going-concern warning after Q2 revenue fell 8.7% to $386 million. First-half losses were $879 million and operating cash outflow $341 million, despite June 30 cash of $1.17 billion and positive working capital of $677 million. It is considering financing including ABS while creditors engage advisers. Fiber sales rose 16% and enabled locations exceeded 3 million, but the rural buildout was not self-funding. An earlier distressed exchange had removed $1.1 billion of debt and brought $3.7 billion of capital without solving the cash-generation problem.

Zhongsheng, an IG Mercedes-Benz dealer, faced possible rating migration. Its 2028 dollar bond yielded over 10% from July, following an 89% first-half profit decline. Revenue fell 18.5%, new-vehicle sales dropped 17.6% to 188,463, and shares lost about 63% this year. S&P rated it one notch above high yield. Cash of 13.6 billion yuan could cover next year's $350 million syndicated loan and 1 billion yuan bond, while repurchases of $117.9 million left about $482 million of the 2028 note outstanding. Liquidity bought time, but the luxury-dealer business remained under pressure.

HDFC dollar notes fell for a fifth session after CEO Sashidhar Jagdishan unexpectedly decided not to seek reappointment. The June 2031 bond reached 98.504 cents, and new August 2029 and 2031 notes their lowest levels. HDFC holds nearly 12% of Indian deposits; its shares fell about 28% this year against a 3.3% Nifty Bank decline. Moody's identified unexpected transition risk but said orderly succession and strategic continuity could contain the credit impact. The issue was leadership confidence rather than the disclosed cash depletion seen at Brightspeed.

China's housing pre-sale reform redirected completion risk. Buyer payments must be escrowed, sales can start only after topping out, and missed delivery allows contract termination and a refund. That protects buyers while removing cheap advance funding from developers, potentially reducing 2027 starts as the grandfathered pipeline runs down. Pre-sales still represented about 75% of new-home transactions at end-2025, although existing-home sales had overtaken new homes. The system is smaller than at the boom peak, when almost 90% of residential floor space was pre-sold, but developers and local governments still face less advance cash and weaker land demand.

## Services, payrolls and long-bond auctions come next

ISM services arrives September 3 at 10 a.m. New York time, with a 54.3 forecast against 54.1 previously. Payrolls follow September 4 at 8:30 a.m.; expectations are for 58,000 jobs after a 23,000 decline and unemployment unchanged at 4.1%. Hiring and service prices will help show whether manufacturing's cost pressure extends broadly enough to sustain near-70% September hike odds.

Thursday's 30-year JGB auction follows the stronger benchmark sale but carries greater fiscal and duration exposure. The September 10 ECB meeting must weigh 3.3% headline inflation against slowing core and services; the September 17–18 BOJ meeting faces near-certain hike pricing and a weak yen. Actual decisions still matter despite how far expectations have moved.

Treasury announces September 3-, 10- and 30-year auction sizes on September 3. Labor Day closes the market September 7, followed by the 3-year sale September 8 and 10-year reopening September 9, when larger buybacks begin. Bidding will show whether higher yields attract private demand alongside the official purchases and competing corporate supply.

section_summaries.section_title: Oil sends the front end lower as September hike odds rise
section_summaries.summary: Oil and breakevens rose together, bringing selling back to policy-sensitive Treasuries. Manufacturing slowed without cost relief, while global funding outcomes remained sharply differentiated.

section_summaries.section_title: Slower manufacturing brings little relief on costs
section_summaries.summary: ISM new orders weakened but input costs and delivery times stayed high. Stable vacancies and Barr's conditional warning supported hike expectations without settling the decision.

section_summaries.section_title: Japan's 3% auction draws buyers as budget requests expand
section_summaries.summary: Japan's 3% benchmark auction attracted better demand. Near-certain hike pricing, a weak yen and larger but non-comparable budget requests left longer-maturity risks unresolved.

section_summaries.section_title: European headline inflation rises as core eases; Israel cuts
section_summaries.summary: European headline inflation rose while core slowed. UK yields climbed despite weaker mortgage demand; Israel cut and Brazil's consumption weakened under high rates.

section_summaries.section_title: Saudi issuance clears; Senegal's IMF agreement brings restructuring closer
section_summaries.summary: Saudi sukuk demand contrasted with Senegal's restructuring repricing. Korea proposed heavy supply, while Canada and domestic-currency markets showed differentiated funding support.

section_summaries.section_title: Credit dispersion reflects different supply, cash-flow and governance risks
section_summaries.summary: Hyperscaler supply differed from Brightspeed's cash burn, Zhongsheng's rating risk and HDFC's succession issue. Chinese pre-sale reform moved completion risk away from buyers.

section_summaries.section_title: Services, payrolls and long-bond auctions come next
section_summaries.summary: Services and payrolls will test hike odds. Long JGB supply, central-bank decisions and Treasury auctions follow before and alongside larger US buybacks.
